ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6538, 31 Dec. 2001, arts. 2, 4, 5, 6, 13 and 15, as last amended by Act No. 18619, 31 Dec. 2021); Presidential Decree on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 25620, 30 Dec. 2014, as amended); Prohibition of Financing for Offenses of Public Intimidation Act (Act No. 6772, 18 Dec. 2002, as amended); Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 5493, 31 Dec. 1997, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, 20 Dec. 1962, arts. 18-23, 39, 46, 175, 287-2 to 287-50 and 543, as amended); Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 15587, 17 May 2018, as amended); Financial Services Commission and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit supervisory regulations on beneficial ownership due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Corporate Registration Extract and Corporate Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry Office, Seoul Central District Court, Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE STATE PATH: Issuer confirms authenticity to the Registrar's signature, then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea affixes an Apostille Certificate. NON-APOSTILLE STATE PATH: Issuer confirms authenticity, then MOFA legalization, then completion of Consular Legalization at the destination state's consulate in Seoul. The two paths are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance Certificate and Corporate Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea and Commercial Registry Office, Seoul Central District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE STATE PATH: NTS and Registry signatures are verified, followed by Apostille issuance by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. NON-APOSTILLE STATE PATH: NTS and Registry signatures are verified, followed by MOFA legalization and then Consular Legalization by the destination state's diplomatic mission in Korea. Only one authentication path applies for the destination state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation, share allotment and execution of Power of Attorney for UBO filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa, with signatory capacity certified by a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE STATE PATH: Board resolution is executed with corporate seal affixed, then Notarization by a Korean Notary Public, then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. NON-APOSTILLE STATE PATH: Notarization by a Korean Notary Public, then MOFA legalization, then Consular Legalization by the destination state's consular authority. Apostille and consular legalization are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Statutory Representative and Incorporator of Yuhan Hoesa, with notarial authentication by a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE STATE PATH: Executed Articles of Association are notarized by a Korean Notary Public, then apostillized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. NON-APOSTILLE STATE PATH: Executed Articles of Association are notarized, then legalized by MOFA, then legalized by the destination state's consulate in Korea. These alternative paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Bank Creditability and Account Relationship Statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Branch Manager of the Korean commercial relationship bank maintaining the Yuhan Hoesa corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: APOSTILLE STATE PATH: Bank officer signature and corporate seal are verified by the bank's legal office, then notarized by a Korean Notary Public, then apostillized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. NON-APOSTILLE STATE PATH: Bank officer signature and corporate seal are verified, notarized, then submitted to MOFA for legalization and thereafter to the destination state's consulate for Consular Legalization. No sequential combination of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation, every director, shareholder, UBO and authorized signatory must be screened continuously against the consolidated OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK HMT sanctions list, and Korean designations under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Foreign Trade Act and FSC/KoFIU administrative orders. The compliance program must run negative news and adverse media checks, identify domestic and foreign politically exposed persons including family members and close associates, apply a cumulative 25% ownership look-through for nominee, trust and legal-arrangement interests, and retain verified records for at least five years. For SWIFT wire and letter-of-credit payment rails, the bank and the company must verify beneficiary ownership, country of destination, embargo status and high-risk counterparty indicators before execution. Any positive match, incomplete UBO certification, or suspected suspicious transaction must trigger an immediate hold and the filing of a suspicious transaction report with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit in accordance with statutory deadlines, followed by enhanced due diligence where the customer is a PEP or a legal person from a high-risk third jurisdiction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iReg) online commercial registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be in Korean language script; foreign names, including the Chinese Baijiu brand name, must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul. The statutory name must follow a four-tier commercial naming convention: first, the distinctive Hangul trade name; second, the phonetic Hangul transliteration of the foreign brand name; third, the registered English-language equivalent; and fourth, any recognized overseas alias used for international trade. The suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' must appear to indicate limited liability. The trade name must not state or suggest a business outside the registered objects, must not be identical to a name already registered with the same or similar business purpose, and must be consistent with the doctrine of commercial reasonableness under the Commercial Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations may be extended by filing a renewal application before the initial 30-day window expires; if the registry rejects a name, the incorporator must, within 14 calendar days of receipt of the written rejection notice, submit a written objection to the Registrar stating the statutory grounds under Articles 18-22 of the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Act. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may file

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-74 (Yuhan Hoesa, or limited liability company); Article 34 (Commercial Registration); Article 35 (Place of Registration); Article 36-2 (Effective Date of Registration); Article 37 (Name Protection and Business Continuity); Commercial Registration Enforcement Rules and Supreme Court Registry Guidelines
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, for Seoul the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division, under the administrative supervision of the Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) prescribed by the Commercial Registration Rules, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Incorporation must state the total capital, which is the aggregate of contributions subscribed by shareholders. In standard registry practice, cash contributions are fully deposited into a domestic bank account opened or designated in the name of the company before the incorporation registration is filed; no blocked governmental escrow account is required. In-kind contributions must be inspected by a licensed expert and completed before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA

WHEREAS, the incorporators of YUHANG HOESA, a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) organized under Articles 287-2 through 287-74 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, have subscribed to the initial paid-in capital in the total amount of KRW [●] required by the Articles of Incorporation, and the said capital has been fully contributed or subscribed as documented in the incorporation records; and

WHEREAS, the Board is authorized by the Articles of Incorporation and by the Commercial Act to confirm the initial capital, adopt the registered office, open the company banking relationship, appoint statutory officers, and execute all filings necessary for incorporation and operational licensing;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUE. The initial subscription and issuance of KRW [●] in capital, divided into [●] shares of identical rights, is hereby approved, ratified, and confirmed. The directors are directed to issue share certificates and to record all shareholdings in the statutorily required share ledger.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office located at [●], Seoul, Republic of Korea, is hereby adopted as the statutory seat of the company. The representative director is directed to register the office, to display the company name, and to maintain the corporate seal, minute book, and statutory records at that address.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Korea-based banking institution [●] is hereby approved as the principal financial institution of the company. The representative director, the chief financial officer, and any two designated signatories are authorized to open domestic settlement, foreign exchange, and trade finance accounts; to execute account facility agreements; and to receive international payments by SWIFT wire transfer, documentary collection, and letter of credit for the export of Chinese baijiu spirits.

4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. The following persons are appointed to the offices indicated: [●] as representative director; [●] as director; [●] as chief financial officer; and [●] as compliance officer. No statutory auditor is required under Article 287-35 of the Commercial Act for the company at this capitalization; if the Articles of Incorporation require an auditor, [●] shall be appointed as statutory auditor by separate written consent.

5. EXECUTION OF STATUTORY AND OPERATIONAL INSTRUMENTS. The representative director and the compliance officer are jointly authorized to prepare, sign, notarize, seal, and submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation, the business registration application, the liquor wholesale license application to the National Tax Service, and all supporting corporate, tax, customs, and licensing documents required for the wholesale export of alcoholic beverages.

6. GENERAL AUTHORITY. Any two officers acting together may execute leases, warehouse agreements, powers of attorney, export contracts, and all ancillary agreements that are prudent and necessary to implement this resolution and to achieve the lawful operation of the company.

7. EFFECTIVENESS. This resolution takes effect immediately and continues in full force until all related registration, tax, customs, and liquor licensing matters are finalized or until the Board adopts a subsequent resolution.

Dated as of [●], [●] month, [●] year.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration preparation, capital contribution, and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Notary Public commissioned in the Republic of Korea, together with a domestic commercial bank selected for the paid-in contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Korean notary to prepare the Articles of Incorporation in full compliance with Commercial Act Articles 287-2 through 287-74. The Articles must precisely state the corporate name, the object clause covering the wholesale and export of Chinese baijiu spirits, the registered office, the amount of capital, the number and class of shares, the method of representation, and any restrictions on share transfers. Each incorporator must sign the subscription schedule. The cash contribution must be deposited into a bank account opened or designated for the company before the final notarization. Obtain a deposit certificate from the bank and have the notary certify the completed subscription. If the registered office is leased, obtain written consent from the building owner and verify that the zoning and building use permit allow a corporate office and spirits wholesale business. The notarized Articles of Incorporation will become the controlling document for the court registration application.
required_dossiers: Passport or Korean resident registration certificate of each incorporator
Articles of Incorporation draft and final notarized version
Share subscription schedule executed by all incorporators
Bank certificate proving deposit of paid-in capital
Certificate of registered office address or owner consent to the lease
Corporate name availability search certificate from the Supreme Court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the bank requires clarification of identity, capital structure, or the registered office, cure the query by correcting the signatures, deposit evidence, or address documents and re-executing the notarization. If the proposed corporate name conflicts with an existing registered name at the name search stage, select a new name and resubmit the search before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation registration application with the District Court Registration Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Division, or the District Court Registration Division with territorial jurisdiction over the company registered office, accessed through the Supreme Court Electronic Registration System (IROS) or in-person counter filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company in the form prescribed by the Commercial Registration Rules. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, proof of full subscription and payment, the written consents appointing directors and the representative director, an inventory of in-kind contributions including the expert appraisal certificate if applicable, and evidence of the registered office. The court registry will examine the submission for formal compliance, issue any supplements, and, once satisfied, record the company in the commercial registry. This registration is the legal birth of the company. Pay the court registration fee measured by the capital amount and obtain the certified corporate registration certificate before proceeding to tax and licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a limited liability company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital subscription ledger and payment deposit certificates
In-kind contribution appraisal report, if applicable
Written appointment or consent of directors and representative director
Registered office ownership or lease consent certificate
Payment receipt for court registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplemental order or suspends the application, cure the stated defects within the statutory correction period, generally two weeks, by filing corrective signatures, revised articles, or proof of payment. If the court questions the registered office or capital contribution, submit lease certificates, bank certificates, photographs of the office, and any explanatory letter by the representative director. An adverse refusal may be appealed under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal registration and business registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local police station for the corporate seal certificate, and the District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office for business registration, filed electronically through the HomeTax Service portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the certified corporate registration certificate, register the corporate seal specimen at the local police station if the company requires a formal seal certificate for banking, tax, and export transactions. Next, submit the business registration application under the Value-Added Tax Act to the district tax office within 20 days of the commencement of business. The application must state the legal entity name, corporate registration number, representative director, registered address, business objective, and the Korean national business classification code corresponding to wholesale of beverages and alcoholic products. Upon approval, the tax office issues the business registration certificate, which is the indispensable precondition for applying for the liquor wholesale license and for opening foreign exchange and trade finance accounts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration issued by the District Court
Corporate seal specimen card and seal registration certificate, if obtained
Copy of representative director identification
Registered office lease agreement or property ownership certificate
Application form for business registration of a corporation
Documents evidencing the company bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local tax office queries the business type or address, revise the application to match the statutory Korean industry classification and HomeTax Service reference data, and resubmit all supporting address and representative documents. If the business registration is suspended, cure the tax office request for supplementary information within the stated deadline or appeal to the National Tax Service Regional Tax Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the liquor wholesale license and alcoholic beverage export authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Liquor Tax Division of the District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office, and Korea Customs Service for export declarations and customs clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal application for a liquor wholesale license under Article 8 of the Liquor Tax Act, together with the certificate of business registration, the corporate registration certificate, evidence of sufficient storage or warehousing arrangements, financial documents showing payment capacity, the lease agreement for the registered office and warehouse if any, and a written compliance plan for age verification and tax recordkeeping. The district tax office will inspect the premises and financial standing before issuing the license. The license must be obtained before any wholesale sale of baijiu in Korea. For export shipments, file the prescribed liquor export declaration with the customs office at the place of departure, and one-time export confirmation with the National Tax Service if required. Maintain complete purchase, storage, sale, and export records for tax audit purposes.
required_dossiers: Liquor wholesale license application form under the Liquor Tax Act
Business registration certificate
Certificate of corporate registration
Warehouse lease or storage facility agreement with floor plan
Financial statements, bank balances, or proof of financial capacity
Letter of consent or lease ownership certificate for the business site
Export declaration form and sales contract for each shipment
Corporate seal certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service issues an information request or additional inspection notice, promptly provide the requested lease, financial, or storage evidence in writing. If the liquor wholesale license is denied, the company may request a reconsideration from the District Tax Office and then appeal to the Regional Tax Office or the National Tax Tribunal within 90 days of the adverse decision. Correct any building permit or storage deficiencies before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and physical licensing, fire safety, and occupational compliance for the export distribution operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Metropolitan Fire and Disaster Headquarters or local fire station, Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency, and Ministry of Environment for any non-industrial environmental registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the company operates only as a spirits export wholesale and distribution business and does not manufacture alcohol, no industrial manufacturing permit or full environmental impact assessment is required. If the company maintains a warehouse or bonded storage facility, secure a fire safety completion inspection certificate under the Act on Fire Prevention and Installations before occupancy, and verify structural load capacity through the building register. Maintain ventilation, fire extinguishers, alarms, and ignition-source controls compatible with high-proof alcohol storage. Install hazardous materials storage equipment and separating walls if the alcohol inventory exceeds the statutory chemical storage thresholds. If the company employs five or more workers, file the initial safety and health report with KOSHA. For export labeling and food sanitation requirements, obtain the appropriate export confirmation from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety for cases involving repacking, labeling, or conditioning of the imported baijiu.
required_dossiers: Fire safety completion inspection certificate for the warehouse or storage premises
Building register and structural load verification documents
Hazardous materials storage compliance documents, if inventory exceeds thresholds
Initial safety and health report to KOSHA, if applicable
Ministry of Food and Drug Safety export confirmation application and label documentation
Certificate of business registration and liquor wholesale license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local fire department refuses to issue the completion certificate, rectify the fire safety defects by installing the required extinguishing systems, emergency exits, ventilation, or hazardous material containment and apply for a re-inspection. If KOSHA requests amendments to the safety and health plan, file an amended report within the stated period. If the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety questions label or content compliance, revise the label, reformat the shipping packaging, or submit the requested laboratory or composition data and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office Liquor Tax Division; Korea Customs Service; Seoul Metropolitan Fire and Disaster Headquarters for storage facilities; Ministry of Food and Drug Safety; and Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency for workplace matters
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Liquor Wholesale License (Article 8, Liquor Tax Act); Liquor Export Declaration and Export Confirmation with the National Tax Service; Foreign Trade Act Exporter Registration, if the company acts as principal exporter; Fire Safety Completion Inspection Certificate for any warehouse; and approved Hazardous Materials Storage Plan, if alcohol inventory exceeds statutory thresholds

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, with delegated administrative work by the Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for the described non-manufacturing spirits export wholesale and distribution operation. No full Environmental Impact Assessment and no Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment are triggered for an ordinary office and dry-goods alcohol warehouse below the statutory development-project thresholds. If a standalone warehouse with a total floor area exceeding 10,000 square metres is later established, an Environmental Registration or environmental preservation plan may be required under the Act on Environmental Impact Assessment and related municipal ordinances.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, no combustion power generation, and no VOC-emitting production process are present in a pure spirits export wholesale business. If limited domestic sanitary wastewater is discharged to public water, it must satisfy the Water Environment Preservation Act effluent standards, including biochemical oxygen demand not exceeding 50 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 60 mg/L, and total suspended solids not exceeding 50 mg/L. Any waste alcohol, damaged or exploded bottles, spill cleanup materials, and alcohol-contaminated packaging materials must be classified as non-hazardous or hazardous waste, as applicable, and managed solely through licensed waste treatment companies under the Waste Control Act. If bulk liquid alcohol is stored above the regulatory threshold, the facility must comply with the Chemical Control Act and National Fire Safety Code requirements for hazardous substances storage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The company must obtain the Fire Safety Completion Inspection Certificate for any warehouse or bonded storage facility, verify the structural load capacity of the building through the official building register, install automatic fire protection systems, emergency exits, ventilation, and ignition-source controls as required by the Act on Fire Prevention and Installations, obtain a Hazardous Materials Storage Permit or submittal if the baijiu inventory in bonded or unbonded warehouses exceeds the statutory thresholds, and file the initial Occupational Safety and Health Report with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency if the company employs five or more workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of Korea National Tax Service (NTS) - HomeTax electronic portal at https://www.hometax.go.kr; export and customs clearance administered by Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS portal at https://unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Korean Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), file an Application for Business Registration with the NTS through HomeTax or with the competent district tax office within 20 days of business commencement; the NTS will issue the 10-digit Korean Business Registration Number, which functions as both the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the VAT registration number. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean place of business, appoint a Korean tax representative, then file the same Application for Business Registration together with the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, foreign tax registration documentation, board resolution, executed power of attorney to the tax representative, evidence of any Korean business premises, and identity documents of the appointed representative with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the tax representative's address. If the foreign non-resident entity has a domestic place of business or is otherwise liable for Korean VAT, it receives the same 10-digit TIN/VAT ID. If the foreign entity merely holds ownership in the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and does not itself make taxable supplies in Korea, it is not required to obtain Korean VAT registration; the Korean LLC is the local tax registrant.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa; the entity is taxed as a domestic corporation on its worldwide income under the Corporate Tax Act. An optional Korean group tax consolidation election may be available under the Corporate Tax Act for qualifying wholly-owned Korean subsidiaries, but it does not alter the entity-level classification of the Yuhan Hoesa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None - VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply by any person commencing a business in Korea under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act, regardless of turnover. A simplified VAT regime exists for certain small individual businesses, but it does not apply to a corporate Yuhan Hoesa and does not exempt any business from the obligation to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All registered businesses must issue tax invoices, and corporations must issue and transmit electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-invoice system no later than the day following issuance. Korea does not operate a real-time per-transaction physical fiscal stamp or cash-register fiscalization system. Instead, the NTS performs central e-invoice clearance and data matching through mandatory electronic tax invoice transmission; the NTS-KCS data interface validates export declarations against export VAT invoices, and any mismatch can trigger an automatic compliance audit. Anti-fraud controls are embedded in the mandatory e-invoice data trail, the export declaration number reconciliation, and the KCS UNI-PASS customs clearance records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21(1) of the Value-Added Tax Act, supplies of goods that are exported are zero-rated at 0% VAT. The VAT-registered exporter must substantiate that Korean customs accepted the export declaration and that the goods physically left Korea. The claim must be supported by an export declaration number shown on the 0% export VAT invoice, a Korea Customs Service export clearance certificate, and bank evidence of actual receipt of foreign currency export proceeds. Qualifying offshore digital services may also be zero-rated when the place of supply is treated as outside Korea and the supplier maintains contemporaneous records showing the non-resident customer, foreign use or consumption, services supplied outside Korea, and payment received from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service (KCS) Export Declaration clearance certificate with the Export Declaration Number issued through UNI-PASS
Signed commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing the physical export of the Chinese Baijiu from Korea
0% VAT export tax invoice transmitted to the NTS through HomeTax
Foreign Exchange Bank certificate / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent foreign exchange settlement receipt

Certificate of Origin, liquor export permit or liquor license evidence under the Liquor Tax Act, and certificate of analysis or alcohol content documentation if required by the destination customs authority
Any destination-country import permit or health certificate required by the importing country before release of the alcohol goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and KCS may audit export zero-rating claims by matching the export declaration, e-tax invoice, bill of lading or air waybill, and foreign exchange settlement records. If a zero-rating claim is unsupported, excessive, or fraudulent, the NTS will claw back the VAT at the standard 10% rate, add late-payment and reporting additional taxes under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, and impose the statutory penalties for false or unissued tax invoices, including the penalty based on the supply value. Criminal liability for tax evasion may also be pursued under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Export proceeds must be repatriated within 180 days of export clearance; failure to do so without prior regulatory approval can result in reversal of the 0% rate, foreign exchange penalties, and customs or tax corrective assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the primary foreign-exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); operational control is delegated to licensed foreign-exchange banks in Korea.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberal current-account convertibility regime. Trade-related payments, service fees, and ordinary profit remittances can flow without transaction-by-transaction approval, provided they are routed through a licensed foreign-exchange bank and the underlying purpose is properly declared. Capital and financial account transactions are more controlled: non-resident equity subscriptions, loans, and cross-border settlements must be notified/reported under FETA, and any inbound foreign investment for Yuhan Hoesa must be filed through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act process before/around capital wiring. Korea does not impose a general surrender requirement on export receipts, but export proceeds must be collected through an authorized foreign-exchange bank within the statutory period. The KRW is not fully internationalized: non-resident access to onshore KRW liquidity, offshore KRW clearing, and speculative local-currency activity is restricted, so cross-border trade settlements are usually denominated in USD or another freely convertible currency. Profit remittances to overseas shareholders are allowed after corporate tax and audit, provided the entity submits an External Transaction Report showing distributable reserves, withholding tax evidence, and board approval. In sum, the currency is operationally convertible for genuine trade and dividends, but compliance with declaration, documentation, and licensed-bank routing is mandatory; no parallel-market or fintech bypass is tolerated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA Article 28, export proceeds must be received and deposited into a domestic foreign-currency account (or an overseas account pre-approved by MOEF) at a licensed foreign-exchange bank within 18 months from the date of export declaration. There is no fixed statutory percentage that must be converted to KRW; 100% of proceeds may be retained in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account as long as the bank records the inflow and matches it to the Korea Customs Service export declaration. Any voluntary conversion into KRW must be executed at the prevailing market rate through the same licensed bank and reported as a foreign-exchange transaction. Documentation for each collection should include the original export LC/contract, invoice, packing list, bill of lading, customs export clearance, and the bank's External Transaction Report entry.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Trade Settlement Account with Online FX Platform

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Revolut, Payoneer, or other foreign payment e-money institutions are not licensed as foreign-exchange banks under Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and cannot lawfully maintain multi-currency operating accounts for a Korean tax-resident company. Domestic fintech banks, such as KakaoBank or Toss Bank, may offer convenient onboarding, but their cross-border trade services and escrow functions are still dependent on a licensed bank or require separate authorization from the Financial Services Commission. For this spirits-export company, the compliance risk of using an unlicensed EMI is unacceptable: AML regulators would question the absence of a Korean External Transaction Report trail, and the bank account would fail to satisfy customs verification and VAT/export evidence requirements. Consequently, the blueprint mandates a Tier-1 commercial bank or its fintech subsidiary that acts merely as a technology front end, never as a licensed settlement bank substitute.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean regulations require the ultimate beneficial owner, statutory officer, or a delegated director with proper power of attorney to complete face-to-face or equivalent identity verification. For a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) with non-resident shareholders, most Tier-1 banks require at least one physical visit by the representative director to the Korean branch to sign account opening documents and undergo the compliance interview. In practice, a remote opening via consular proxy is sometimes accepted if the power of attorney is notarized at a Korean embassy/consulate, apostilled/legalized, translated into Korean by a licensed translator, and accompanied by certified passport copies; however, the bank still requires video-call confirmation and may refuse if the proxy cannot answer detailed KYC questions about the business. Therefore, the likely mandate is physical appearance for the first account opening, followed by remote management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and opaque beneficial ownership of the Yuhan Hoesa LLC structure, combined with high-value cross-border alcohol distribution, may trigger a high-risk enhanced due diligence rating.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified company registry excerpt (deed of incorporation), shareholders register, UBO declaration naming all natural persons with more than 25% ownership, passport copies of the directors, tax residency certificates, six-month bank references from the shareholders' primary banks, source-of-wealth statements, and an organizational chart of the Chinese baijiu supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag arising from merchandise sourced in China, shipped through Korea, and sold to third-country buyers, with potential invoice/price manipulation or mismatched HS codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete contract chain: Chinese supplier export contract, Korean import purchase order, international sales contracts with final buyers, matched commercial invoices and packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, Korea Customs Service import/export declarations, pre-shipment inspection certificates, warehouse storage receipts, insurance certificates, and a documented gross-margin calculation that is commercially logical for wholesale liquor distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk product classification: alcoholic beverages require statutory licensing and create a reputation risk if the distributor is linked to unapproved brands, counterfeit products, or illegal re-export to sanctionable territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Korean Liquor Tax Act wholesale/manufacturing license, original brand authorization or exclusive distribution agreement from the baijiu producer, trademark registration evidence, food safety and quality inspection reports, including alcohol strength, additives, and production date, certificate of origin, allergen/label compliance declarations, and a clear end-market list confirming no sales to OFAC/EU/UN-sanctioned jurisdictions or unauthorized resellers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected transaction profile: if the company requests third-party payments, prepayments to suppliers, or cash-based disbursements before the bank understands the working capital cycle, the bank may file a Suspicious Transaction Report.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a 12-month projected cash-flow and transaction-flow chart showing each expected inbound LC/MT103 and each outbound supplier wire; a board-approved anti-money laundering and know-your-customer policy; sample invoices; corporate VAT registrations; details of all existing bank facilities; and a written undertaking that all settlements will be made only between the counterparty's bank account in the contract and the company's account, with no cash or third-party topping.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The investment must be disclosed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before the transfer. For a non-resident shareholder injecting equity into Yuhan Hoesa, the recipient company opens a dedicated Capital Escrow Account at a licensed foreign-exchange bank, and the investor wires USD or another convertible currency using SWIFT MT103 with the purpose code declared as inbound foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Notice. The bank verifies the investment notification filed with KOTRA/MOEF, credits the escrow account, issues a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate after funds are actually received, and then transfers the amount into the operational KRW account after conversion or into a foreign-currency account as the company directs. The capital verification is evidenced by the foreign-exchange bank's certificate of receipt, BOK transaction records, and the external capital investment report. The company must not use the injected capital for speculative local financial products before the regulatory notification is accepted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating payments such as purchasing Chinese baijiu from suppliers or paying freight, warehousing, and logistics costs, the company should use bank-executed SWIFT MT103 wires with the correct Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code, such as general trade payment for importing goods/services, attaching the underlying invoice/contract and customs declaration. For sales to overseas distributors, the exporter may request an irrevocable at-sight Letter of Credit, which is advised and confirmed through the Korean negotiating bank; the bank forwards the shipping documents under UCP600, negotiates the proceeds, and deposits them into the exporter's foreign-currency account. Documentary collections, such as D/P or D/A, are acceptable for established counterparties, but the bank must receive the collection instructions and present documents through the collecting bank. All outbound disbursements should be tagged with the purchase order or LC number and reconciled against Korea Customs Service export/import declarations to preserve the audit trail for VAT and corporate tax purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts (USD/KRW and CNY/KRW) with a licensed foreign-exchange bank, executed solely to hedge documented underlying trade receivables/payables and limited to the real-demand amount.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for non-resident or offshore counterparties, but a Korean resident company can use an NDF only with a licensed bank and must prove a genuine exposure when the onshore deliverable market is constrained; speculative NDF positions are prohibited.

Cross-currency swaps for working-capital risk management between foreign investment capital (USD) and KRW operating liquidity, provided the bank confirms matching principal/no arbitrage and underlying trade or loan exposure.

Plain-vanilla currency options (call/put on USD/KRW or CNY/KRW) as hedges against adverse FX moves on forecast trade flows, with option premiums not classified as speculative if they are consistent with the company's hedging policy and underlying trade forecast.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Members and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members' Meeting of the Yuhan Hoesa; minutes maintained at the registered office and available for inspection; no filing to the Commercial Registration Court unless articles are amended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year, being 31 March for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing fee; failure to convene the members' meeting and approve the annual settlement is a default of the Commercial Act that may expose directors and the representative to administrative fines; continued corporate dormancy is a ground for judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off by the tax authority

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) through the competent local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 March; a 1-month extension may be allowed for statutory reasons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the assessed tax (40% for failure to report) plus late payment interest of approximately 0.022% per day; persistent non-payment permits the NTS to close the business registration and seek a court order for compulsory dissolution/strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government authority (Si/Gun/Gu) via the local e-tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the same date as the national corporate income tax return, normally within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay attracts local tax delinquency charges, including a 3% non-payment penalty and additional monthly overdue charges on the unpaid surtax; chronic local tax arrears can support an action for involuntary dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Return and Export Zero-Rated Refund Claim for Spirits Export
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General VAT taxpayers file preliminary returns for January-March by 25 April and July-September by 25 October, and final semi-annual returns for January-June by 25 July and July-December by 25 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a VAT return triggers a 20% penalty on the assessed VAT and may delay export zero-rating refunds; repeated non-filing allows the NTS to revoke the business registration and initiates administrative strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent Statutory External Audit Report (conditional on legal thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system; audit report also presented to the Members' Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The certified auditor must complete and report within 3 months of fiscal year-end and before the annual members' meeting; the audit report must be submitted to the Financial Services Commission without delay after issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a registered CPA auditor when required, or failure to submit the audit report, is subject to administrative fines, regulatory sanctions, restriction of tax incentives, and referral by the financial authorities to the court for serious governance failures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Change Report and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (conditional on foreign shareholding)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA); beneficial ownership information must be reconfirmed by financial institutions under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Foreign-invested foreign ownership changes, equity transfers, capital changes, or corporate detail changes must be reported within 30 days of the relevant event; no annual confirmation is required unless a change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted foreign investment change reports are subject to administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 (about USD 3,700); inaccurate UBO records can also draw monetary penalties and criminal fines under Korean anti-money-laundering legislation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Liquor Wholesale License Annual Sales Summary and Continued Compliance Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent National Tax Service tax office holding the liquor wholesale record under the Liquor Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual liquor sales and inventory summary for the preceding calendar year must be submitted by 31 January; in addition, monthly liquor sales records are due on the 25th day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual summary or maintain the statutory liquor ledger can result in suspension or revocation of the liquor wholesale licence; an inactive licence is administratively forfeited and the underlying corporate registration may be struck off if the company ceases to operate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: On-Site Inspection and Maintenance of Statutory Corporate Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of the Yuhan Hoesa; no annual filing to the court, but records must be present and inspectable at the office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous availability during business hours; a full internal register audit should be completed before the annual members' meeting and no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or false statutory registers expose the company and its directors to administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700); irreparable non-compliance supports administrative strike-off while the court supervises dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Presidential Decree when: (1) the entity is listed or registered on a Korean securities exchange; (2) total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end reach or exceed KRW 12 billion, roughly USD 9.1 million; (3) the company is classified as a public-interest company by the Financial Services Commission, including criteria of total assets or annual revenue of at least KRW 100 billion and 1,000 or more regular employees; or (4) the Financial Services Commission designates the company as requiring external audit because of size, debt, industry impact, or public-interest exposure. A Yuhan Hoesa must also be audited if it is a foreign-invested company exceeding the same quantitative thresholds or if the foreign investor is required by a bank or an investment regulator to present audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for public-interest and listed companies; non-listed private limited companies such as a Yuhan Hoesa may use Korean GAAP (General Accounting Standards) unless K-IFRS is voluntarily adopted. All statutory audits must be performed in accordance with the Korean Standards on Auditing and the External Audit and Accounting Standards set by the Financial Services Commission.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a separate central annual UBO filing for a private Yuhan Hoesa. Beneficial ownership is established in the Register of Members, and any transfer of shares or equity interest must be reflected in that register. For a foreign-invested company, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires a change report to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of an equity transfer or any other change in foreign shareholding. Korean financial institutions subject to anti-money-laundering rules must reconfirm the beneficial owner on an annual basis or at account renewal, and any person becoming a 30-day reporting-transfer counterpart must complete the relevant share-register transfer before receiving membership rights.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 2,500 per year for registered office, company secretary and statutory document custody services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 25,000 for a small or medium unlisted LLC, increasing with export turnover, related-party entities, and K-IFRS consolidated reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate income tax holiday for liquor export distributors. Targeted incentives under the Special Tax Cases Control Act include SME tax reductions, regional investment tax credits, and employment tax credits. Free Economic Zone enterprises may receive local tax reductions and customs duty exemptions. R&D tax credits are available for qualifying technological development activities, but a pure wholesale distribution entity is unlikely to qualify. No patent box regime applies to distribution activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for the Business Year (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system. Local income tax surtax is filed through the provincial/local government WeTax system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year. For a December 31 fiscal-year-end entity, the return is due by March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension may be granted for foreign-invested companies; further extensions are available upon application to the NTS for entities with overseas fiscal years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and business registration number: entity legal name, head office address, representative director, business registration number (사업자등록번호), and filing period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the 10-digit Korean business registration number exactly as issued by the competent district tax office. For a non-resident controlled Yuhan Hoesa, the Korean entity is a domestic corporation and must not be treated as a non-resident. Ensure the representative director's foreign address, passport number, and foreign resident ID are correctly reported; failure to update changes is an omission that can attract minor penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year beginning and ending dates, accounting basis, industry code, and business classification (ISIC 4632 - wholesale of alcohol; NAICS 424820).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the fiscal year consistent with the entity's financial statements. If the foreign parent uses a different year-end, the Korean entity must still file on its own fiscal year. Cross-border intercompany transactions spanning different fiscal years must be adjusted to the Korean entity's year for TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet figures: total assets, total liabilities, capital stock, capital surplus, retained earnings, and total equity as of fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report under K-IFRS or Korean GAAP. In a related-party financing context, if non-resident loans exceed the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalization threshold (3:1 for financial companies), the interest on the excess is non-deductible. Disclose all loans from foreign shareholders in the related-party transaction summary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement: total gross revenue, including domestic and export sales, and all other operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all global export wholesale revenue from baijiu sales. Gross revenue should exclude VAT but include excise taxes, if any. Export sales supported by customs declarations, bills of lading, letters of credit, and SWIFT records. Improper exclusion of export revenue is a common audit red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: inventory at beginning, purchases from related and unrelated parties, import duties, freight, handling, labor, depreciation, manufacturing overhead, and ending inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases of baijiu from the Chinese parent must be at arm's length. Maintain a full transfer pricing study with comparable margins for wholesale distributors. Custom duties paid on importation into Korea form part of inventory cost; do not double-count. Re-export goods via bonded warehouses must follow customs procedures to support cost deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses: commission, marketing, packaging design, logistics, agency fees, rent, payroll, insurance, professional fees, royalties, and interest expense.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to foreign affiliates must satisfy the 'actual services rendered' standard. A commission or service fee paid without evidence of service delivery and tangible benefit is treated as non-deductible and recharacterized as dividend or income subject to withholding. Interest paid to non-resident creditors is subject to thin capitalization and WHT; verify DTA rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses added back: taxes and surcharges, fines and penalties, bribes, non-qualifying entertainment expenses, and expenses lacking proper documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean tax law denies deductions for fines, criminal and administrative penalties, and entertainment exceeding statutory limits. Cross-border sale commissions to procurement officers are regarded as bribery if not legitimate; they are non-deductible and may trigger the Foreign Bribery Prevention Act and personal criminal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income and non-taxable income adjustments: dividends from foreign subsidiaries may be deductible under the intercorporate dividend exemption, and certain foreign-source income may be exempted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the exporter also owns foreign subsidiaries, verify conditions under the STCA for the dividend exemption or indirect foreign tax credit. A minimum 10% capital ownership and six-month holding period are required; attach foreign financial statements and tax receipts. For a simple wholesale exporter, this box is usually empty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base (taxable income) before additional tax reductions: total income minus non-deductible additions, non-taxable exclusions, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the taxable base after transfer pricing adjustments. If the NTS later reassesses an arm's length price, the taxpayer can still file a corrected return. Loss carryforwards are limited to 5 years; if the company undergoes a merger or more than 50% ownership change, continuity of business rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculation using progressive brackets: 10% up to KRW 200 million; 20% up to KRW 20 billion; 22% up to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply progressive rates accurately. For foreign investors computing provisional income for DTA or TRC purposes, remember the local income tax surtax is an additional 10% of national CIT, making the top combined effective rate 24%. For small export SMEs under KRW 200 million profit, the effective combined rate is 11%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: foreign tax credit, R&D credit, employment credit, facility investment credit, and other tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credit on foreign-source income subject to Korean tax, including foreign withholding on export commissions or royalties. The credit is limited to Korean tax attributable to that foreign income. If foreign tax exceeds the Korean tax, the excess is not credited but should be reclaimed in the source country. Attach NTS foreign tax credit schedules and evidence of tax paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Minimum corporate tax, alternative minimum tax for large corporations, and final CIT computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Even if regular tax is reduced by credits, a minimum tax of 10% of taxable income after exemptions may apply for large corporations. Export distributors with heavy foreign tax credits should ensure they are not under the minimum tax threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid corporate tax, interim tax payments, and withholding tax credits applied against the annual CIT liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile interim tax payments made in July (within 2 months of the first half). If the actual annual tax exceeds prepayments, a penalty may be assessed. Export entities with volatile revenue should adjust interim prepayments using the actual-half-year method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surtax (지방소득세) filed as a separate return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the local surtax alongside the national CIT in WeTax. The local surtax is 10% of the national CIT payable. Non-resident shareholders are not directly taxed on this local surtax; it is borne by the Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International related-party transaction disclosure (국제거래명세서), including purchase, sales, loans, royalty, and service transactions with foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory attach when annual international related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion. Transfer pricing documentation (Local File, Master File, and CbCR where applicable) must be retained. Failure to attach the disclosure can trigger a 20% negligence penalty on the transaction amount and unjust deduction assessments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 20% of unpaid tax for failure to file an actual return. If fraudulent or grossly negligent failure to file, an additional 10% applies. For under-reporting taxable income, a 10% penalty on the understated tax; for dishonest under-reporting, a 40% penalty applies. Daily late-payment interest charges: 0.025% per day from the statutory due date (annualized approximately 9.125%). Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to 5 times the evaded tax; for evasion exceeding KRW 500 million, up to 7 years imprisonment. Cross-border tax evasion may trigger NTS criminal referral and Interpol red notice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a DTA, the Korean payer must withhold at the statutory 22% unless the non-resident recipient provides, before the filing due date of the withholding return: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the recipient's tax authority for the relevant fiscal year; (ii) a Certificate of Beneficial Ownership confirming the recipient is the actual owner of the income; (iii) a statement of no Korean permanent establishment; (iv) a completed NTS form for reduced treaty withholding (서면 제출); (v) for dividends, evidence that the recipient holds at least the treaty-required shareholding percentage for the minimum holding period (e.g., 25% shareholding for the reduced China-Korea DTA rate); and (vi) any additional LOB/PPT declarations. If the recipient does not provide these documents before the payment, the payer must withhold at the statutory rate. The non-resident may file a claim for tax treaty adjustment or a refund with the NTS within 3 years from the statutory filing deadline. The NTS may deny treaty benefits if the recipient is a conduit or shell company without economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident for use of IP in Korea: statutory WHT is 22% (20% CIT plus 2% local surtax). Under typical DTA rates: royalties may be reduced to 10% or 15%. For China-Korea DTA, royalties for the use of trademarks, software, or know-how are generally taxable at 10% (or 0% for copyright royalties other than cinematograph films). Interest paid to non-resident shareholders or third parties: statutory WHT is 22%; China-Korea DTA rate for interest is generally 10%. Interest paid to financial institutions may be 0% or 5% under certain treaties. Substantiation of exempt/reduced rates requires TRC and beneficial ownership evidence. Intercompany loans must observe arm's length interest rates under Korean TP rules; excessive interest is non-deductible under thin capitalization.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in total international related-party transactions during the fiscal year for Local File; KRW 100 billion in consolidated revenue of the multinational group and the Korean entity's related-party transaction amount exceeding KRW 10 billion for Master File; KRW 50 billion for CbCR; even where the mandatory threshold is not breached, the NTS may request TP documentation when a tax risk is identified.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has not enacted OECD-form Economic Substance Regulations, but the substance-over-form principle and anti-abuse rules apply under the Corporate Tax Act and International Tax Adjustment Act. A liquid export distributor must demonstrate active economic substance through its employees, office premises, warehousing, logistics functions, customer contracts, invoicing, inventory movement, and risk-bearing capacity. If a non-resident parent or Chinese affiliate controls sales, orders, pricing, and risk, the Korean entity may be deemed a limited-risk distributor and its profits adjusted to the arm's length remuneration. The NTS may also disregard shell entities for treaty purposes under the Limitation of Benefits and Principal Purpose Test provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a paper entity without any substantive business activity, employees, office, warehouse, or inventory. It is used solely to invoice baijiu export transactions and to flow revenue to a low-tax foreign entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Corporate Tax Act assessment procedures, the NTS will deny deductions, recharacterize transactions, impose the 40% dishonest underreporting penalty, and disallow treaty benefits under the International Tax Adjustment Act LOB/PPT provisions. The local tax surtax penalty is also assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly establish or operate a sham entity may suffer piercing of the corporate veil under commercial and tort principles, becoming personally liable for unpaid corporate tax, local tax, and penalties where assets insufficient. Criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act carries imprisonment up to 5 years; where tax evaded exceeds KRW 500 million, imprisonment up to 7 years. Directors may be subject to travel bans, blacklisting, and disqualification from serving on any Korean board.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany purchase prices for baijiu from a related Chinese manufacturer are set artificially high to shift Korean profit offshore, or the Korean entity pays excessive royalties or marketing fees to the foreign parent without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS can make a transfer pricing adjustment under the International Tax Adjustment Act, impose a 20% penalty on unjustified underreporting (or 40% if fraudulent), add daily late-payment interest, and disallow tax treaty benefits. If the transaction is not disclosed, a 10% negligence penalty applies on the transaction amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed off on contrived intercompany contracts and knowingly caused the understatement are jointly and severally liable to the extent of corporate underpayment. Criminal tax evasion sanctions apply: imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to 5 times the tax; in severe cross-border schemes, up to 7 years. Directors can be blacklisted and temporarily prohibited from departing Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity pays dividends, interest, or royalties to a Hong Kong or other conduit company that is not the ultimate beneficial owner, for the purpose of obtaining a reduced DTA withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will deny the treaty rate, collect the full 22% statutory WHT, impose underreporting penalties of up to 40%, and apply daily late-payment interest. The payor may also be liable for failure to withhold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who arranged the conduit structure may be criminally prosecuted for fraud in withholding remittance, with imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil liability extends to the withholding shortfall, penalties, and tax attorney costs. A director who is a non-resident may be issued an Interpol red notice or extradition request where fraud is established.
